description: Change of use of 23 Hackney Grove from F1 to C3 to provide 5 self-contained dwellings, involving part-demolition, ground floor extension, and a mansard roof extension. Demolition of Vernon Hall and construction of a part-1, part-4 storey building comprising 3 self-contained dwellings (C3), with associated cycle parking and refuse stores.
decision_conditions: <p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, details and full specifications of 2 swift bricks/boxes, and 2 bat boxes/bricks, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:</p><ul><li>A minimum of 2 swift bricks (same requirements for swift box) incorporated into the design of the development. They should be installed in groups of at least 2, and placed at or close to eaves level of the development hereby approved. They should be placed at least 5m above the ground with a 5m unobstructed flight path, both below and in front of the swift brick. The swift brick should be located facing north, east, or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided) and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Where possible, swift bricks should be set flush into the external wall to match adjacent brickwork.</li><li>A minimum of 2 bat boxes and/or bricks incorporated into the design of the development. Boxes should be placed at or close to the eaves level of the development and at least 4m above the ground. The boxes should be placed away from artificial light sources and ideally located near dark tree lines or hedgerows where possible. The boxes should be located facing south, southeast or southwest, and exposed to sun for part of the day.</li></ul><p>The details hereby approved shall be delivered, in full, prior to the first occupation of the development and shall be maintained for the lifespan of the development.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To support bird and bat populations, including swifts, in Hackney and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing nesting opportunities, in accordance with Hackney’s Local Plan LP33 policy LP47 which states that all development schemes involving buildings with an eaves height or roof commencement height of 5 metres and above are required to provide nesting boxes for swifts, sparrows, starlings, and/or bats as appropriate.</p>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial;">Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, notwithstanding the details as shown on the approved drawings, precise details of the proposed cycle parking provision which is safe, secure and accessible for all shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained solely for its designated use.<br><br>REASON: To ensure adequate provision for the safe and secure storage of bicycles, to promote sustainable modes of transport and in the interest of safeguarding highway safety in accordance with Policy LP42 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</span></p>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial;">Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, notwithstanding the details as shown on the approved drawings, precise details of the proposed refuse and recycling storage capacity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details and the area shall remain free from obstruction other than for its approved use.<br><br>REASON: To ensure adequate provision for refuse and recycling is provided which would safeguard the amenity of the area and not compromise pedestrian safety.</span></p>

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>A post installation test shall be carried out prior to occupation to demonstrate that all residential premises designed in accordance with “BS8233:2014 - Guidance on Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings” achieving the required internal noise levels have been met and the results submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To obtain required sound insulation and prevent noise nuisance.</p>

<div class="gmail_default" style="">Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved,&nbsp; Demolition and Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall be in full accordance with Hackney Council’s Code of Construction Practice, the Mayor of London's Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, and relevant IAQM guidance.The development shall be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved Plan throughout the entire construction period, which must cover all phases of development and include:</div><div class="gmail_default" style=""><br></div><ul><li>An introduction with project description, management responsibilities, site working hours, a named point of contact for residents, and clear community communication procedures (such as newsletters and fliers).</li><li>Full details of site logistics, delivery locations, the size and daily frequency of vehicles, site access/turning arrangements, any required parking suspensions, and strict measures to prevent the deposit of mud and debris on the public highway.</li><li>An air quality and dust management plan incorporating a construction dust risk assessment, alongside details of resource management, waste control, and dust mitigation during site clearance, demolition, and construction (including any concrete crushing or activities requiring an environmental permit).</li><li>A detailed construction programme identifying activities likely to cause high levels of noise or dust, coupled with a separate noise/vibration monitoring and management scheme developed by a suitably qualified person to demonstrate Best Practicable Means (BPM) and safeguard local sensitive receptors.</li></ul><div class="gmail_default">The construction shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details unless the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority is received for any variation.</div><div class="gmail_default" style=""><br></div><div class="gmail_default" style="">REASON: To protect air quality, public safety, and human health by minimising emissions of air pollution, dust, noise, and vibration during demolition and construction; to ensure minimal nuisance, disturbance, or detriment is caused to the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the area generally; and to avoid hazard, obstruction, or damage being caused to users of the public highway network.</div>

<p>Prior to commencement of works, full details and specifications of the biosolar roof(s) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submission shall include the following:</p><ul><li>Detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof including location of PV panels, roof lights and access points where applicable, and their relationship with the green roof;</li><li>The design of the biosolar roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</li><li>Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of 80mm for a sedum roof, 100mm for extensive roofs, and 100mm–150mm for wildflower species;</li><li>Details of the proposed type of invertebrate habitat with a minimum of one feature per 30m2; which could include areas of bare, unplanted substrates, log piles, boulder or stone piles, sand piles;</li><li>Details of the drainage system for the roof;</li><li>Details of the planting mix;</li><li>Including a minimum of 16+ species for wildflower/extensive roof;</li><li>Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and</li><li>general maintenance actions of biosolar roof;</li><li>For biosolar roofs, provide details on how the roof's design meets fire and building safety requirements;</li><li>Roof plan layout including access points, fire breaks, and lighting.</li></ul><p>Within a month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority that the green roof(s) has been delivered in line with the approved details unless otherwise agreed in writing. The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs, in line with Hackney's Local Plan LP33, policy LP46.</p>

<p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To protect acceptable local noise levels.</p>

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work, the applicant shall submit, and have approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, a detailed layout, cross sections (scale 1:20), full specifications and a detailed management and maintenance plan of the biodiverse roof with a minimum substrate depth of 80mm, not including the vegetative mat. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: &nbsp;In the interest of enhancing biodiversity and managing flood risk and providing a sustainable drainage system.</p>

<p>A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the site and in the lower ground floor against surface water (overland flow) flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the basement is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with BS 8102:2009 code of practice for "protection of below ground structures against water from the ground" and current best practice where applicable.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: In the interest of sustainable urban drainage.</p>
